Markets.title: US debt tops $40 trillion: Chris Wood flags the 5% trigger that could rattle stock market
Markets.summary: US public debt has surpassed $40 trillion amid a worsening fiscal position. Jefferies strategist Christopher Wood warns that if the 10-year Treasury yield climbs above 5%, it could trigger turmoil in the stock market.

Markets.title: RailTel shares rise 4% after securing Rs 165 crore order from Western Coalfields
Markets.summary: RailTel Corporation of India shares rose nearly 4% after winning a Rs 164.79 crore work order from Western Coalfields Limited. This contract involves setting up an MPLS VPN network for 60 months, bringing the company's total August order wins to five worth approximately Rs 551.44 crore.

Markets.title: Hindustan Zinc shares jump 7% in two sessions. What’s triggering the rally?
Markets.summary: Hindustan Zinc shares jumped 7% over two sessions as silver prices continued to climb. The rally was further supported by strong company fundamentals, including a 145% year-over-year surge in Q1 FY27 net profit to Rs 5,469 crore.

Markets.title: Augmont Enterprises raises Rs 246.29 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
Markets.summary: Augmont Enterprises raised Rs 246.29 crore by allotting 31.25 lakh shares to 14 anchor investors ahead of its IPO. The Rs 825-crore public offering, which includes a fresh issue and an offer for sale, opens on August 21.

Markets.title: Did Goodluck India shares really crash 66% in just one day? Here's how the bonus math works
Markets.summary: Goodluck India shares appeared to crash 66% in a single day due to an adjustment for the company's 2:1 bonus issue. However, the stock was actually down only about 4% on an adjusted basis.

Markets.title: Gold prices rise Rs 6,400/10g in 3 days; silver jumps Rs 13,000/kg despite Middle East tensions. Big rally brewing?
Markets.summary: Gold and silver prices on the MCX rose for the third consecutive session, driven by a weaker U.S. dollar and expectations of controlled Treasury yields. Over a three-day period, silver surged by Rs 13,000 per kilogram and gold gained nearly Rs 6,500 per 10 grams amid ongoing market uncertainty.

Geo-Political.title: UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada condemn Israel's West Bank settlement project
Geo-Political.summary: The UK, France, Germany, Italy, and Canada condemned Israel's plans to expand settlements in the occupied West Bank. This joint opposition increases international pressure on the Israeli government regarding the strategically vital territory.

Geo-Political.title: How much could Trump's 'economic D-Day' hurt Iran?
Geo-Political.summary: Iran has historically found ways to evade punishing economic sanctions. It remains uncertain how much damage a new "economic D-Day" proposed by Trump would inflict on the Iranian economy.

Geo-Political.title: El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office
Geo-Political.summary: Scientists report that a strengthening El Niño weather pattern is an unprecedented event. This pattern is expected to make 2027 the hottest year on record globally.

Geo-Political.title: British rapper Yung Filly to face retrial on rape charges in Australia
Geo-Political.summary: British rapper and YouTuber Yung Filly was cleared of several sexual assault offences by an Australian jury last month. However, he faces a retrial because the jury could not reach a decision on three remaining rape charges.

Geo-Political.title: Why the US economy is ringing alarm bells
Geo-Political.summary: The United States recently reached a significant national debt milestone, raising concerns about the health and stability of the world's largest economy. Analysts are debating the severity of these fiscal issues and evaluating how worried global markets should be about the situation.

Geo-Political.title: Hong Kong's Tiananmen activists guilty in national security trial
Geo-Political.summary: Three prominent Hong Kong activists have been found guilty of inciting subversion under a strict national security law introduced by China. The charges stem from their involvement in organizing and promoting annual vigils commemorating the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown.

Data & Insights.summary: India has reduced its sugar import duty to zero to help lower record-high domestic prices. This action follows earlier government measures that banned sugar exports and tightened stock holding limits.

Data & Insights.summary: India's core infrastructure sector growth slowed to 5.4% in July from a revised 6% in June. The expansion was primarily driven by the iron ore, cement, and electricity sectors.

Data & Insights.title: RBI’s $50 billion boost may not be enough to lift the rupee | Here's why
Data & Insights.summary: India expects a $50 billion balance-of-payments surplus in fiscal year 2027, but experts warn this may not strengthen the rupee. The currency's impact depends on whether the central bank absorbs these inflows as reserves or allows them to enter the market.

Data & Insights.title: RBI's rate-setting panel hints at future policy tightening if inflation persists
Data & Insights.summary: RBI Governor Malhotra stated that the central bank requires clearer evidence of persistent high inflation before acting. Consequently, the rate-setting panel indicated potential future policy tightening if price pressures continue.

Data & Insights.title: Who pays, who profits — The economics of India's toll highways landscape
Data & Insights.summary: Data from the Indian Highway Management Company shows how high-traffic routes and the FASTag annual pass are shaping highway revenues. The findings highlight the evolving economics of toll roads and shifting private sector involvement in India's highway network.

India.summary: Rajneesh Yadav, the state topper of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Board's Uttar Madhyama examination, had his exam results cancelled due to document fraud. Authorities have also ordered the recovery of the award he received.

India.summary: The UPSC Civil Services Mains 2026 exam has officially begun with the essay paper. Candidates must arrive early at the exam venue to complete face authentication, identity verification, and frisking.

India.title: Don't Issue New SIMs To Those Having 9 Connections: Centre Asks Telcos
India.summary: The Indian government has directed telecom companies to stop issuing new SIM cards to individuals who already have nine mobile connections. This measure is designed to help operators identify and block customers attempting to exceed the legal limit for mobile subscriptions.
